column1: # tests/expected-diff.tsv — the registry of INTENTIONAL behavior changes (D-04)
# tests/scenarios/differential.sh runs a binary built from the pinned
# milestone-start commit db057e7ebbd21e0a7256dcd7c1b26ff3870a5478 and a binary
# built from the current tree over the same read and --dry-run command matrix,
# each against its own fresh temp HOME, and compares four fields: stdout,
# stderr, exit_code, and the resulting filesystem tree. Any difference fails the
# scenario unless a row in this file names it.
# FORMAT — three tab-separated columns, no quoting:
#   command<TAB>field<TAB>reason
#   command   the matrix entry verbatim, exactly as differential.sh lists it,
#             e.g. `sync status --json` (no leading `dot`, no --home)
#   field     one of: stdout  stderr  exit_code  tree
#   reason    free prose — what changed, and why someone decided to change it
# Lines beginning with # are comments. Blank lines are ignored.
# WHAT THIS FILE IS
# A changelog of intentional behavior changes across a milestone whose declared
# default is behavior preservation. Its length is itself the signal: this file
# is meant to stay short, and a long one means the milestone has drifted from
# its own premise. Read it top to bottom before trusting a green differential.
# WHAT THIS FILE IS NOT
# It is not a suppression list. A row added to turn a red build green — rather
# than to record a change someone deliberately made — has inverted this file's
# purpose. If the harness goes red and nobody decided to change that behavior,
# the finding is a regression: fix the code, do not add a row.
# TWO RULES THE SCENARIO ENFORCES, SO THEY CANNOT ROT INTO CONVENTION
#   1. `version` must never appear here. Both binaries are built with identical
#      -ldflags (VERSION=diff COMMIT=diff) and an explicitly pinned GOTOOLCHAIN,
#      so their version output is normalized at the build step. A version diff
#      means that normalization broke — a build problem, not a behavior change.
#      The scenario rejects a `version` row outright.
#   2. A row whose difference stops occurring fails the scenario with a
#      remove-this-row message. When the change a row records is reverted or
#      superseded, the row goes with it; the registry prunes itself instead of
#      accumulating dead excuses.
# This file shipped with zero data rows: the milestone started from a stated
# position of full behavior preservation. Phase 5 is the one phase that changes
# behavior on purpose, and the rows below are its record.
# READING THE `tree` ROWS ON A DEVELOPER MACHINE
# differential.sh disables the tree field entirely on any host carrying a
# Homebrew prefix (see its TREE_COMPARISON preflight), because read-only brew
# probes write into the sandbox HOME and refetch over the network. A tree row
# therefore matches nothing on such a host, and the run reports it in a third
# state - neither pass nor fail - on a line beginning with `~` that names the
# row and says the field was not compared. Those rows are NOT stale and must not
# be removed on that evidence: the run never looked at them. The run also prints
# how many rows it could not assert and states that it is therefore not a full
# verification. CI's linux job runs this scenario in a clean ubuntu:22.04
# container with no Homebrew prefix, compares the tree unconditionally, and is
# the authoritative run.
# The third state is scoped to the field THIS RUN skipped, not to the field
# name. A `tree` row on a host that did compare the tree still fails with the
# remove-this-row message, exactly like every other field, so rule 2 above is
# unweakened for anything the run actually compared.
# command
apply --profile minimal --yes --dry-run
